minutes.headline: Water District held a special meeting vote on borrowing to fund a PFAS treatment plant; result not confirmed in captions
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District held a special district meeting on a single article: authorizing borrowing to fund a PFAS water treatment plant and related well/transmission-main work, prompted by violations found in the district's 2026 DEP sanitary survey. Numerous residents raised concerns about cost, alternatives (point-of-use filters, a Townsend interconnection), and whether the district's DEP filings accurately described the urgency, before voters cast a clicker vote whose outcome the captions do not state.

what_happened.line: Water District voters held a special-meeting clicker vote on borrowing for a PFAS treatment plant; the outcome was not confirmed in captions.
The borrowing article followed PFAS and manganese violations found in the district's 2026 DEP sanitary survey.
A commissioner said the district compared buying water from Townsend against building its own plant and found the costs roughly comparable, favoring its own supply.
Residents questioned the accuracy of the district's DEP filing and pressed for a full cost breakdown, including future rate impacts, before voting.
A commissioner said he would look into whether adjusting well operations could reduce PFAS levels further, with the superintendent and district engineers.

why_it_matters: This borrowing question could affect water district rates and how the PFAS treatment plant and related well work get funded going forward.
Several residents tied this spending decision to the town's recent failed override votes and school staffing cuts, framing it as a competing-priorities question rather than a water-only decision.
A resident's unanswered question about a discrepancy between the district's DEP filing and its underlying data went unresolved at the meeting.
